rows.title: /* eslint-disable-next-line no-unused-vars */  will disappear when save
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the sample. The retest above shows that running `eslint --fix` outside VS Code removes the same comment. Your configuration disables the base `no-unused-vars` rule and enables `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars`, so the original comment suppresses nothing and ESLint removes it as an unused directive.

Use `/* eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars */` above the variable instead. If you want to preserve unused directives project-wide, set `linterOptions: { reportUnusedDisableDirectives: 'off' }` in `eslint.config.ts`. Both options were verified against your sample: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/2108#issuecomment-5697321171.

This resolves the report as a configuration question rather than an extension defect.

rows.title: docs: Document for `eslint.lintTask.command` is missing
ESLint plugin breaks when using `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the additional detail. Your follow-up gives us a concrete reproduction: enable `eslint.lintTask.enable`, set `eslint.lintTask.command` to `yarn eslint`, and run the whole-folder task before opening any files. That task parses terminal output using VS Code's `$eslint-stylish` problem matcher, unlike normal per-file linting. The log shows multiline React Hooks messages with rule codes on later lines, which the matcher cannot capture and which interrupt its parsing of subsequent errors. This points to task-output handling rather than the rules failing to run. The related multiline matcher request is https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/9635, but this ESLint-specific case should remain open until the handling is resolved.

rows.title: File exists, but `ENOENT: no such file or directory...` reported.
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and the follow-up details. This failure path was fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/d8214448aa1ba338c84184239bfee66cea24fbaa: errors from `fs.realpathSync.native` are now caught, and the server continues with the original file path rather than dropping linting with an unhandled `ENOENT`. The fix shipped in ESLint extension 2.4.2 and remains in current releases, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in release/2.4.2.
rows.verifyEvidence: The report's stack trace is an unhandled ENOENT thrown by fs.realpathSync.native in getFileSystemPath; the diff wraps exactly that call in try/catch, so linting proceeds instead of failing silently.

I'll consolidate this there so the long-path and `realpath` investigation stays in one place.

rows.title: Do not lint outside current project workspace directory
Feature request: Provide a way to control files fixed during onCodeActionsSave (e.g., ignorePatterns)
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the request. This is now supported through `eslint.codeActionsOnSave.options`, which was added in extension 3.0.16. That setting is passed as a separate ESLint options object when fixes are computed on save, so you can use `ignorePatterns` there to exclude files from fix-on-save without excluding them from normal validation. You can also use `overrideConfigFile` if maintaining a dedicated save-time ESLint configuration is a better fit. The implementation is in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/6f8769b072debf9ac124b55893dbc19e1bf8795d. The fix shipped in release/3.0.16.
rows.verifyEvidence: The commit adds `eslint.codeActionsOnSave.options`, spreading an arbitrary ESLint class options object (including ignorePatterns/ignorePath) into the save-time fix run, delivering the requested per-save ignore control generically.

rows.title: When the user provides eslint.options, remove the requirement for a eslint.config.js file
respect estlint-suppressions.json
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and discussion. Bulk-suppression support has now shipped in stable version 3.0.34. With ESLint 10.1 or newer, use `eslint.bulkSuppression.enable` to apply the suppression file and surface suppressed violations at the severity selected by `eslint.bulkSuppression.severity`; `eslint.bulkSuppression.location` supports a non-default file path. If suppressed violations should be hidden entirely, `eslint.options` can pass `applySuppressions: true` without enabling their diagnostic display. The implementation landed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/9d33f02b2ddaadc55f7f30dfd2338ccca12dc798. The fix shipped in release/3.0.34.
rows.verifyEvidence: Suppressions are only applied when the opt-in eslint.bulkSuppression.enable setting is on (default false, 'no behavior change'), so by default the extension still ignores eslint-suppressions.json as the issue requested.

Extension should report config file errors
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. Invalid ESLint configurations are reported through VS Code's language status indicator for the affected document, with the detailed error available in the `ESLint` output channel. The same request was reviewed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/issues/1402#issuecomment-3645936662, where that presentation was confirmed as the recommended VS Code behavior. Reporting a precise diagnostic on `eslint.config.mjs` would also require ESLint to provide a reliable source location, which runtime configuration errors generally do not include.

rows.title: ESLint version 10.0.3 only supports flat configs. Setting is ignored
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and investigation. This was a spurious message caused by the default value of `eslint.experimental.useFlatConfig` being sent as though it had been explicitly configured. It was fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/pull/2172 in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-eslint/commit/5a2809ce452e41c84747b86a0334734e87e9c87b. The fix first shipped in pre-release 3.0.25 and is included in stable release 3.0.34. The fix shipped in release/3.0.34.
rows.verifyEvidence: The client previously always sent experimental.useFlatConfig defaulting to false, triggering the server's `=== false` warning branch; the diff sends it undefined when unset and warns only on explicit settings.

rows.title: GitHub Copilot Chat interrupting workflow
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the context. This request is about GitHub Copilot Chat's terminal-command approval and permission model, rather than the ESLint extension. Since no change in this repository can provide those controls, I'm closing this as out of scope for vscode-eslint.
